newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks jump at opening after Friday drop.
newsitem.headline: French stocks jump at opening after Friday drop.

text.p: French shares started with a jump on Monday, in line with other European markets, in a rebound from Friday's sharp 2.26 percent drop.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 20.62 points or 0.92 percent at 2,261.34 at 0906 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract rose to 2,264 from 2,239 at Friday's close.
A first resistance level at 2,245.36 was quickly broken and the next levels are seen at 2,261/62 and later 2,284.96.
Dealers said many investors would probably remain sidelined for the rest of 1996, having taken profits on Friday on a 19 percent gain in the CAC-40 for the year.
"It will take several days to recover," said a dealer. "Trade will be quiet for a while, with the U.S. producer price index (coming out) on Wednesday and consumer price index on Thursday," he added.
The data may give some indication whether the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee, meeting on December 17, will raise rates.

Club Med shares jumped 6.21 percent to 336.50 francs after the resort company's large shareholders put an end on Friday to a 1990 shareholders' agreement, making it easier for them to sell and making the company more vulnerable to a takeover bid.
Eurotunnel shares gained 2.17 percent to 7.05 francs after announcing a rise in November traffic and reiterating that service wil restart on December 10.
Thomson-CSF shares rose 1.77 percent to 167.00 francs on expectation of a new offer for the company, as part of the Thomson privatisation, that would lead to a minority buyout.
